Selection was made against the latest City main: MB-001 migration is complete and unclaimed for verification (Mech is not its migration host), MB-003 is claimed by Alien and MB-004 depends on MB-003, so sequence order selects MB-005. Implementation branch mission/MB-005-host-health created from utopia main c7ef3cd1c6be0155332d03afc3607dfdbf49c205.

Parity oracle established. The donor is TypeScript with zero runtime dependencies; installing typescript 5.7.2 into the git-ignored donor checkout and running its own tsc produced lib/**/*.js (31 files) that executes on plain Node. That gives an executable golden reference: the ported Utopia module can be differential-tested against the donor implementation on identical synthetic inputs, which is far stronger parity evidence than ported test vectors alone. The donor's own tests also run against this build.

TEST_FAIL: three root capability tests hard-coded manifest positions. tests/capability-registry.test.mjs used m.districts[0] and m.districts[2] and asserted an absolute unbridged count of 1; tests/capability-adapters.test.mjs used manifest.districts[0] and asserted catalog.length===6 and 5 AVAILABLE. Declaring the new 02-engineering/03-host-health-station building changed the census, so all three failed. This is the same class of fragile fixture that MB-002 already had to repair, and it is a latent defect on main that every future Mission declaring a district or building would trip. Failure receipt: .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-005/run-1/tests/root-tests-before.txt

REPAIR_APPLIED: made the three fixtures census-relative instead of position-dependent. They now use m.districts.at(-1) for the district under test, count unbridged capabilities relative to a baseline taken before the fixture mutates the manifest, and assert added-parser entries by capabilityId suffix rather than by absolute catalog size. The properties under test are unchanged - qualified identity per district/building/module, pending state for an unbridged module, and that all five bridged adapters still execute - but they can no longer break merely because a later Mission declares another district or building. After the repair pnpm test is 58/58 and node city/test-all.mjs is 212/212.

OWNER_INTERVENTION: real donor bug found and deliberately NOT fixed. dsh-health-scheduler src/core/bands.ts bandKeyOf() never returns :warn for a lower-is-worse metric, because rampEndpoints returns best>worst for that polarity so the second test (value <= worst) is unreachable. Reproduced against the compiled donor: bandKeyOf('recovery_rate', 0.6, {warn:0.8,critical:0.3}) === 'recovery_rate:critical' when it should be ':warn'. higher-is-worse is unaffected. Effect: for those metrics the band clock starts at the warn endpoint, so crossing warn->critical already satisfies the sustain gate. CHOICE: port it exactly and pin it with a naming test, because MIGRATION_ONLY forbids changing donor semantics and a silent fix would break differential parity and change when a gate opens. RECOMMENDATION: the City owner needs a superseding decision before this is treated as intended; the fix is two lines but it is a behaviour change. Recorded in DONOR.json donorBugsFound.
